Independent Research (single author); disclaimer: author employed by Google Research, views his own

Proposes an approach — end-to-end spec-first architecture for agent-authored, formally verified software (five pillars), illustrated by two case studies whose figures are declared illustrative; defines a planned readability experiment (protocol frozen, not run). Paper: 'This paper is a proposal'

Spec-First Agentic Engineering architecture (no version): five pillars: (1) spec as source of truth (code and proofs as disposable build outputs); (2) zero human code review gated by CI; (3) Verification IR (VIR) lowered by a thin verified translator; (4) extensional Computational Type Theory (CTT) specs + HOAS in the VIR; (5) two-tier agent fleet (Personal Spec-Copilots + Shared Synthesis Fleet). Builds on author's salt, SaltBench, x86lean, MetaPRL

Modular formal specifications (CTT) and a Shared Domain Ontology as primary human artefacts; three channels: Functional Spec, Cost and Resource Spec (hard gates), Implementation Directives (untrusted 1-line hints); agent-generated VIR and proof certificates; TCB Debt Ledger; change scorecard

Engineer writes/edits spec (helped by Spec-Copilot) -> agent synthesises VIR + proofs from spec conjunction -> automated CI gates (proof kernel/zero-axiom/well-formedness, vacuity, adversarial mutation, litmus vectors, telemetry) -> human reviews spec diff + scorecard -> thin verified lowering to machine code. Org level: Shared Fleet checks semantic merge conflicts; proof-timeout escalation. Adoption roadmap Phases 1-3

Humans review only public module boundary specification diffs, shared ontology and automated telemetry/scorecard; no review of implementation or proof scripts ('zero human code review'); gates run before the human opens the change; human-audited HAL for hardware boundary
